Teams moving to Taskflow from another tracker want to bring their issues into a project in one go. Build the backend of the bulk import.

User story: as someone who may create issues in a project, I upload a file. The client parses it into rows and sends them along with a key that identifies that upload. Every row becomes an issue in the project, in file order.

Add exactly these exports:

1. `src/schemas/issue-import.ts`:

```ts
export const importIssueRowSchema = z.object({
  title: z.string().min(3).max(200),
  description: z.string().max(20_000).nullable().default(null),
  status: issueStatusSchema.default("backlog"),
  priority: issuePrioritySchema.default("none"),
  assigneeEmail: emailSchema.nullable().default(null),
  labels: z.array(z.string().min(1).max(40)).max(20).default([]),
  dueAt: isoTimestampSchema.nullable().default(null),
});

export const importIssuesSchema = z.object({
  orgId: orgIdSchema,
  projectId: projectIdSchema,
  importKey: z.string().min(8).max(64),
  rows: z.array(importIssueRowSchema).min(1).max(500),
});

export type ImportIssueRowInput = z.infer<typeof importIssueRowSchema>;
export type ImportIssuesInput = z.infer<typeof importIssuesSchema>;
```

2. In `src/types/issue.ts`:

```ts
export interface IssueImportResult {
  readonly importKey: string;
  readonly projectId: ProjectId;
  readonly issues: readonly Issue[];   // in file order
  readonly replayed: boolean;          // true when the key had been imported before
}
```

3. In `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`: `export async function importIssues(actor: Actor, input: ImportIssuesInput): Promise<IssueImportResult>`.

4. A new domain event `issues.imported` in `TaskflowEventMap`: `EventEnvelope & { projectId: ProjectId; importKey: string; issueIds: readonly IssueId[] }`, with `issueIds` in file order and published on behalf of the importer.

Acceptance behaviour

- Access: importing needs the same permission as creating an issue in that project. An `orgId` outside the actor's workspace → `TenantScopeError`; an unknown project, including a project of another workspace → `NotFoundError` (the one in `src/server/services/_support.ts`); an archived project → `AlreadyArchivedError`. A refused import creates nothing.
- All or nothing. The import is checked before anything is written. The plan's per-project issue quota applies to the whole batch: if the project's issues plus the rows would go over the plan's per-project limit, the whole import is refused with an error and nothing is created — the refusal is the same one a single create at the limit gets, and the issues are counted the same way. The batch also spends the workspace's issue-creation rate allowance, one unit per row, before anything is written; when the allowance does not cover the batch, the import is refused and nothing is created. A refused import does not use up its key: the same key uploaded again later is treated as a first upload.
- Rows: title, description, status, priority and due date exactly as given; the importer is the author; no parent and no estimate. Imported issues are numbered in file order, continuing after the highest number the project has ever used, and issues created afterwards continue after them.
- Assignee: `assigneeEmail` is matched, case-insensitively, against the email addresses of the workspace's current active members. An address that is not one of them — unknown, belonging to someone who is not a member of this workspace, or to a member who has been removed — leaves the issue unassigned. That is never an error.
- Labels: each name in `labels` is matched exactly (case-sensitively) against the workspace's own labels. A name that does not exist yet is created — once, however many rows use it — with the default colour and no description, and the issue carries every label named for it (a name repeated inside one row counts once). Labels of other workspaces are never involved, whatever their names.
- Replays: uploading a key this workspace has already imported returns the result of that first import — the same issues, in the same order, with `replayed: true` — and creates nothing, whatever the rows now say. A different key is a new import even when the rows are identical. Keys are per workspace: the same key in another workspace is unrelated. Replays must work across restarts, so imports are persisted; a freshly migrated database (the way the test suite builds one) must have whatever you add.
- Announcements: a successful import publishes exactly one `issues.imported` event for the batch and no `issue.created`; a replay publishes nothing. The batch event must give the product everything the per-issue announcements would have: the imported issues are searchable right away; the workspace's issues-used meter rises by the number of imported issues and agrees with a full recount; the audit log gets exactly one entry for the import — action `issues.imported`, recorded as the importer's action, subject kind `project`, subject id and project id the project's, metadata `{ count, importKey }` — and no per-issue entries. Nobody is notified about imported issues (an assignee is not told), and no outgoing webhook delivery is created for them, even for endpoints that subscribe to issue events. The hidden test attaches the application's event handlers exactly as the server does at start-up.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	/**
     2	 * Issue rows: the widest query surface in the app. Every method takes `orgId` first and honours `IssueFilter.includeArchived`.
     3	 *
     4	 * Must call (do not reimplement): archivePatch, restorePatch, shouldFilterArchived
     5	 */
     6	import {
     7	  and,
     8	  count,
     9	  desc,
    10	  eq,
    11	  inArray,
    12	  isNotNull,
    13	  isNull,
    14	  like,
    15	  lt,
    16	  or,
    17	  sql,
    18	} from "drizzle-orm";
    19	import { newId } from "@/lib/id";
    20	import {
    21	  archivePatch,
    22	  restorePatch,
    23	  shouldFilterArchived,
    24	} from "@/lib/soft-delete";
    25	import { attachments, comments, getDb, issueLabels, issues } from "@/server/db";
    26	import { ISSUE_STATUSES } from "@/types/issue";
    27	import { toIsoTimestamp } from "@/types/common";
    28	import { livePredicate, orgPredicate } from "./base-repository";
    29	import { compact, keysetPredicate, probeLimit, toPage } from "./_paging";
    30	import { toIssue } from "./_mappers";
    31	import { listLabelsForIssues } from "./label-repository";
    32	import type {
    33	  CreateIssueInput,
    34	  IssueFilterInput,
    35	  UpdateIssueInput,
    36	} from "@/schemas/issue";
    37	import type {
    38	  ArchiveScope,
    39	  IsoTimestamp,
    40	  IssueId,
    41	  LabelId,
    42	  OrgId,
    43	  Page,
    44	  ProjectId,
    45	  UserId,
    46	} from "@/types/common";
    47	import type {
    48	  Issue,
    49	  IssueBoardColumn,
    50	  IssueStatus,
    51	  IssueWithRelations,
    52	} from "@/types/issue";
    53	import type { SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
    54	
    55	/** Statuses whose entry stamps `completed_at`; leaving one clears it again. */
    56	const TERMINAL_STATUSES: readonly IssueStatus[] = ["done", "canceled"];
    57	
    58	export async function findIssueById(
    59	  orgId: OrgId,
    60	  issueId: IssueId,
    61	): Promise<Issue | null> {
    62	  const row = getDb()
    63	    .select()
    64	    .from(issues)
    65	    .where(and(orgPredicate(issues.orgId, orgId), eq(issues.id, issueId)))
    66	    .get();
    67	  if (!row) return null;
    68	
    69	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(orgId, [row.id as IssueId]);
    70	  return toIssue(row, (labels[row.id] ?? []).map((label) => label.id));
    71	}
    72	
    73	export async function findIssueByNumber(
    74	  orgId: OrgId,
    75	  projectId: ProjectId,
    76	  issueNumber: number,
    77	): Promise<Issue | null> {
    78	  const row = getDb()
    79	    .select()
    80	    .from(issues)
    81	    .where(
    82	      and(
    83	        orgPredicate(issues.orgId, orgId),
    84	        eq(issues.projectId, projectId),
    85	        eq(issues.number, issueNumber),
    86	      ),
    87	    )
    88	    .get();
    89	  return row ? toIssue(row) : null;
    90	}
    91	
    92	/** Builds the shared predicate list behind `listIssues` and its count. */
    93	function issueFilters(input: IssueFilterInput): readonly SQL[] {
    94	  const scope: ArchiveScope = shouldFilterArchived(input)
    95	    ? {}
    96	    : { includeArchived: true };
    97	
    98	  return compact(
    99	    orgPredicate(issues.orgId, input.orgId),
   100	    livePredicate(issues.archivedAt, scope),
   101	    input.projectId === undefined
   102	      ? undefined
   103	      : eq(issues.projectId, input.projectId),
   104	    input.status === undefined || input.status.length === 0
   105	      ? undefined
   106	      : inArray(issues.status, [...input.status]),
   107	    input.priority === undefined || input.priority.length === 0
   108	      ? undefined
   109	      : inArray(issues.priority, [...input.priority]),
   110	    input.assigneeId === undefined
   111	      ? undefined
   112	      : input.assigneeId === null
   113	        ? isNull(issues.assigneeId)
   114	        : eq(issues.assigneeId, input.assigneeId),
   115	    input.authorId === undefined
   116	      ? undefined
   117	      : eq(issues.authorId, input.authorId),
   118	    input.dueBefore === undefined ? undefined : lt(issues.dueAt, input.dueBefore),
   119	    input.query === undefined
   120	      ? undefined
   121	      : or(
   122	          like(issues.title, `%${input.query}%`),
   123	          like(issues.description, `%${input.query}%`),
   124	        ),
   125	    input.labelIds === undefined || input.labelIds.length === 0
   126	      ? undefined
   127	      : inArray(
   128	          issues.id,
   129	          getDb()
   130	            .select({ id: issueLabels.issueId })
   131	            .from(issueLabels)
   132	            .where(
   133	              and(
   134	                orgPredicate(issueLabels.orgId, input.orgId),
   135	                inArray(issueLabels.labelId, [...input.labelIds]),
   136	              ),
   137	            ),
   138	        ),
   139	  );
   140	}
   141	
   142	export async function listIssues(
   143	  input: IssueFilterInput,
   144	): Promise<Page<Issue>> {
   145	  const db = getDb();
   146	  const filters = issueFilters(input);
   147	  const sort = { sortColumn: issues.createdAt, idColumn: issues.id };
   148	
   149	  const total = db
   150	    .select({ value: count() })
   151	    .from(issues)
   152	    .where(and(...filters))
   153	    .get();
   154	
   155	  const rows = db
   156	    .select()
   157	    .from(issues)
   158	    .where(and(...filters, ...compact(keysetPredicate(sort, input.cursor))))
   159	    .orderBy(desc(issues.createdAt), desc(issues.id))
   160	    .limit(probeLimit(input.limit))
   161	    .all();
   162	
   163	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(
   164	    input.orgId,
   165	    rows.map((row) => row.id as IssueId),
   166	  );
   167	
   168	  return toPage(
   169	    rows,
   170	    input.limit,
   171	    total?.value ?? 0,
   172	    (row) => toIssue(row, (labels[row.id] ?? []).map((label) => label.id)),
   173	    (row) => ({ id: row.id, sortValue: row.createdAt }),
   174	  );
   175	}
   176	
   177	/**
   178	 * The list view needs comment and attachment counts per row. Two grouped
   179	 * queries beat N+1 round trips, so the counts are folded in afterwards.
   180	 */
   181	export async function listIssuesWithRelations(
   182	  input: IssueFilterInput,
   183	): Promise<Page<IssueWithRelations>> {
   184	  const db = getDb();
   185	  const page = await listIssues(input);
   186	  const ids = page.items.map((issue) => issue.id);
   187	  if (ids.length === 0) {
   188	    return { items: [], nextCursor: page.nextCursor, total: page.total };
   189	  }
   190	
   191	  const commentCounts = db
   192	    .select({ issueId: comments.issueId, value: count() })
   193	    .from(comments)
   194	    .where(
   195	      and(
   196	        orgPredicate(comments.orgId, input.orgId),
   197	        inArray(comments.issueId, [...ids]),
   198	        isNull(comments.archivedAt),
   199	      ),
   200	    )
   201	    .groupBy(comments.issueId)
   202	    .all();
   203	
   204	  const attachmentCounts = db
   205	    .select({ issueId: attachments.issueId, value: count() })
   206	    .from(attachments)
   207	    .where(
   208	      and(
   209	        orgPredicate(attachments.orgId, input.orgId),
   210	        inArray(attachments.issueId, [...ids]),
   211	      ),
   212	    )
   213	    .groupBy(attachments.issueId)
   214	    .all();
   215	
   216	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(input.orgId, ids);
   217	  const commentsBy = new Map(commentCounts.map((r) => [r.issueId, r.value]));
   218	  const attachmentsBy = new Map(
   219	    attachmentCounts.map((r) => [r.issueId, r.value]),
   220	  );
   221	
   222	  return {
   223	    items: page.items.map((issue) => ({
   224	      issue,
   225	      labels: labels[issue.id] ?? [],
   226	      commentCount: commentsBy.get(issue.id) ?? 0,
   227	      attachmentCount: attachmentsBy.get(issue.id) ?? 0,
   228	    })),
   229	    nextCursor: page.nextCursor,
   230	    total: page.total,
   231	  };
   232	}
   233	
   234	/** One column per status, in `ISSUE_STATUSES` order, live rows only. */
   235	export async function listBoardColumns(
   236	  orgId: OrgId,
   237	  projectId: ProjectId,
   238	): Promise<readonly IssueBoardColumn[]> {
   239	  const rows = getDb()
   240	    .select()
   241	    .from(issues)
   242	    .where(
   243	      and(
   244	        ...compact(
   245	          orgPredicate(issues.orgId, orgId),
   246	          eq(issues.projectId, projectId),
   247	          livePredicate(issues.archivedAt, {}),
   248	        ),
   249	      ),
   250	    )
   251	    .orderBy(desc(issues.updatedAt))
   252	    .all();
   253	
   254	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(
   255	    orgId,
   256	    rows.map((row) => row.id as IssueId),
   257	  );
   258	
   259	  return ISSUE_STATUSES.map((status) => {
   260	    const column = rows
   261	      .filter((row) => row.status === status)
   262	      .map((row) => toIssue(row, (labels[row.id] ?? []).map((l) => l.id)));
   263	    return { status, issues: column, total: column.length };
   264	  });
   265	}

   267	export async function countIssues(
   268	  orgId: OrgId,
   269	  projectId: ProjectId,
   270	  scope: ArchiveScope = {},
   271	): Promise<number> {
   272	  const row = getDb()
   273	    .select({ value: count() })
   274	    .from(issues)
   275	    .where(
   276	      and(
   277	        ...compact(
   278	          orgPredicate(issues.orgId, orgId),
   279	          eq(issues.projectId, projectId),
   280	          livePredicate(issues.archivedAt, scope),
   281	        ),

   288	/**

   292	export async function nextIssueNumber(

   298	    .from(issues)
   299	    .where(

   306	export async function insertIssue(
   307	  input: CreateIssueInput,
   308	  authorId: UserId,
   309	  issueNumber: number,
   310	): Promise<Issue> {
   311	  const stamp = toIsoTimestamp(new Date());
   312	  const db = getDb();
   313	
   314	  const row = db
   315	    .insert(issues)
   316	    .values({
   317	      id: newId(),
   318	      orgId: input.orgId,
   319	      projectId: input.projectId,
   320	      number: issueNumber,
   321	      title: input.title,
   322	      description: input.description,
   323	      status: input.status,
   324	      priority: input.priority,
   325	      authorId,
   326	      assigneeId: input.assigneeId,
   327	      parentId: input.parentId,
   328	      estimate: input.estimate,
   329	      dueAt: input.dueAt,
   330	      startedAt: null,
   331	      completedAt: null,
   332	      createdAt: stamp,
   333	      updatedAt: stamp,
   334	    })
   335	    .returning()
   336	    .get();

   338	  if (input.labelIds.length > 0) {
   339	    db.insert(issueLabels)
   340	      .values(
   341	        input.labelIds.map((labelId) => ({

   353	export async function updateIssue(input: UpdateIssueInput): Promise<Issue> {

   355	  const row = db
   356	    .update(issues)
   357	    .set({
   358	      ...(input.title === undefined ? {} : { title: input.title }),

   389	        .values(
